reviews.comment: *Phil 336, wasn't an option. This guy is just spectacular. Incredibly wise, incredibly caring, stop by his office hours once a month and you'll be golden. Show up, listen to what he says, and you got it. The topics are NOT easy and it can be confusing at times, but he cares so much and is so knowledgeable, wants to help you.
Very easy professor for PHIL 111. You're graded primarily on a presentation and a written exam, so ensure you show up for those. The exam was primarily over the textbook, but the final was very easy.

I took him for HONR 101, and he was a very insightful and inspirational professor. Every week, you have to read an article or a few chapters before class and then we discuss the reading. It's student led discussions, but he'll jump in to ask questions or clarify. It's an easy A if you participate.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was overall okay; I just didn't like how disorganized he was online, especially during the summer. I didn't like how he would grade and make comments about why he took off points for little things. I really tried to learn overall about the class after watching his lecture videos, but I would fall asleep. Didn't really enjoy the class tbh.

10 out of 10!  Took this professor for summer 2 session and still was able to enjoy my summer. Gives great feedback to your work for CRIJ 3302..Not a tough grader and records his lectures while he is teaching so feels like you are apart of the classroom.  Would def. recommend and take again.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: such a sweet professor. he genuinely made me interested in phil. i thought about doing a phil minor because of him lmao. his lectures are actually interesting, and hes passionate and knowledgable. dont slack on the group presentation or the essay because it drops your grade. no exams besides the final. REALLY study the quizzes for the final iykwim
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't recommend. We are graded on very few items but the items we are graded on are weighted heavily. Made an 80 on a presentation even though we followed his feedback beforehand and now my grade is stuck at a B. Haven't taken the final yet but it's 30% of our grade and we have no previous exams to help us know what to expect.

The goat. Dr. Koepsell's class is very discussion based, and he makes sure to remember everyone's names and encourage participation. Attendance isn't mandatory (about half the class showed up), but his lectures are always fun and engaging. There's 1 essay, 1 project, and a final, with a couple of quizzes, all of which are pretty easy.

Dr. Koepsell is a thoughtful professor who provides a great introduction to philosophy. His lectures are interesting, and, although attendance isn't required, you need to come because the quizzes sometimes cover the lectures. Otherwise, there's an essay, presentation, and final which are all graded fairly. I highly recommend taking him if you can.

Dr. Koepsell is an amazing lecturer & well rounded professional who knows how to "dumb down" philosophical concepts and apply them to everyday life. Most of the tested content is from lectures, so be sure to take good notes. There are weekly quizzes, but the overall grade is mostly based on a presentation, an in-class essay, and the final.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can't say enough good things about him. This is the second time I have taken a class from him, and I will take another if I can. Above anything, he wants his students to succeed. He's easily accessible outside of class and will work with you if you communicate with him.

Professor Koepsell is a good professor, but by the end of the semester, your entire grade hangs in the balance of three major assignments: two finals (one essay, one multiple-choice) and one research paper. All of this accounts for 60% of your grade, and it is all due during the last week of school. He is a good professor but be prepared to work.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would 110% take David Koepsell again. He is so understanding and makes a point to try to get to know all of his students. I looked forward to his class (which says a lot lol). If you put in the effort an A is totally doable!

As interesting as the class was and engaging the lectures were, I don't think he's a good essay grader at all. I genuinely thought I made a good essay, only for him to give me a C. I sent him drafts to practice for the real one and took the exact advice he told me. I was really hoping for an A. He wouldn't know a good essay if it slapped him.

Great prof. Cool guy, pretty reasonable and understanding. Engaging and interesting lectures but I didn't go bc it was 8am. Quizzes are not bad just use the textbook. Essay not bad either. No exams except for final, just old quiz questions, super easy.

Dr Koepsell has been one of my favorite philosophy professors so far. His lectures were really interesting and super informative. If you pay attention and read outside of class you will learn a lot. Quizzes once a week, 10 minute presentation, in class essay and a final. Pay attention in class, take notes and read. All it takes to pass.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVE Koepsell. Based on past reviews on here he took feedback and changed his curriculum. Go to class, take notes, make outlines before the in-class essays, and use your resources for the final and you will do fine! Learned so many interesting things, and still reference them in my daily life.

He really likes what he teaches but it can be difficult for an A, final exam was extremely difficult even with notes worth 60% of our grade. Class is simple but he words things oddly which can make it more challenging.

He is pretty chill if you're looking for an easy credit course. Beware of In Class Essays they are graded heavily so I recommend him if you're good at writing essays also the final exam is pretty difficult even with open notes. Overall pretty decent professor.

Professor Koepsell is one of the kindest professors I have come across. He cares about student success and it shows. The only negative thing I have to say if that the final was pretty difficult. Graded on multiple quizzes, two short essays you write in class, and a final exam. Learned a lot of interesting material!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Koepsell is awesome. He really cares about his students. Your grade is based on 10 quizzes, 2 in class essays, and a final. He is easy to reach and gives good feedback on the essays. Lecture was always interesting and he often ties in pop-culture references. If you love Breaking Bad, he'll give a lecture on it at the end of the semester!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about the topics, and wants his students to be successful. Put in the effort required and you should do well.

Dr. Koepsell is an amazing professor! His lectures are engaging as he asks us questions and incorporates a lot of pop culture references to make the course very relatable. Your grade is based on quizzes, two in-class essays, a participation grade, and a final. He is very approachable and genuinely wants to help students learn. If you can, take him!

Dr. Koepsell is an amazing and thoughtful professor. I took him for 334 and 332 and he has definitely made a positive impact on my education. He is genuinely amazing at lecturing and making the information digestible to us. He's also just super interesting and a very fun prof.

Professor Koepsell is a great person and you can tell he is very passionate about the subject. His class is easy if you put in the work. The course grade is composed of weekly quizzes, two essays, and a final exam.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet guy! But your grade is only based on 3 assignments that have very little guidelines. One bad grade can really plummet your overall grade. Don't be afraid to ask him questions and for guidance on assignments, he will point you in the right direction. The final exam was very lecture heavy so take good notes.

Unhelpful feedback/critiques on assignments and unclear grading criteria. Gives little to no insight on how to improve assignment and then gives a bad grade. Exam was lecture heavy with many contradictory questions/answers. Lectures can be boring and feel pointless. All grades were determined in the last month or so. 
Have fun!

From the previous rates I figured this would be a good class to take with all of my other courses and work loads. I was really hoping for an A, but ended with a B. There were only 3 grades in this class and the grading is a little vague.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

teacherNote.comment: I appreciate the feedback and am sorry you had some trouble due to too few graded assignments. I'm using this input to improve the course and address these concerns.

reviews.comment: This prof was absolutely booty. His handwriting is terrible so taking notes in class is very difficult. His class is unstructured and more of a conversation so it becomes very confusing what exactly to write. I read the entire textbook and 50% of the questions on the final came from his notes. He is a nice man but not suited to be a professor.

teacherNote.comment: I appreciate this feedback. I'm updating the syllabus for more frequent and less weighty assignments for grading, and will type my notes for future lectures. I'm sorry you had such a tough time with these issues.

reviews.comment: Dr. Koepsell was a great professor! He is passionate about the material and pretty fun to listen to. There are no posted notes, and everything comes from the textbook so READ! There's a group project, an essay, and one (cumulative) exam. The project wasn't too bad, and it's an open topic. The essay was time-consuming. Final exam is kinda hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Koepsell is one of my favorite professors I've taken at A&M. He understands the class is required for most non-phil majors but works to engage his students and keep them interested. You are graded on very little, but he was very generous with grading and is willing to work with you if you communicate your grade goals with him. TAKE HIM!

I stopped regularly attending classes about halfway through, but just cause it was an 8am. I read the book instead and I was fine. His lectures were very interesting and he worked to engage his students by asking questions and asking for opinions. Weekly quizzes, one project, essay, and a final. You'll get a good grade if you follow the rubric.

Professor Koepsell was a fantastic professor, his lectures were more conversations of what we thought about philosophical ideas rather than being talked at for an hour. For me, he graded very generously on the assignments in this class (which was only one paper and a presentation). Make sure you take good notes in class the lectures aren't online.
So caring. Amazing and nice guy. Was a bit disorganized and we were graded on very little but I learned a lot. Get the book. I didn't and wish I did. His lectures are hard to take notes over.

Dr. Koepsell had the most interesting and engaging lectures I've ever had. My only issue was with his grading/grading scale, especially for what is an introductory class. 3 assignments worth 30% each- project, paper, and final- and 10% attendance. The paper wasn't graded by the final, so 70% of our grade was left unknown. Amazing guy, super nice.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures
